newsitem.title: USA: JonBenet Ramsey's body had cord wrapped round neck.
newsitem.headline: JonBenet Ramsey's body had cord wrapped round neck.

text.p: JonBenet Ramsey, the murdered 6-year-old beauty pageant winner, had a white cord wrapped around her neck tied to a stick with the word "Korea" printed in gold, according to an autopsy report released on Wednesday.
However, the report did not fill in a key blank in the murder mystery -- the time of death.
The report also did not say whether the child had been sexually molested, although her underwear, which was urine-stained, also contained "red areas of staining" in the crotch.

The wooden stick that was attached to the cord around her neck was "irregularly broken at both ends and there are several colors of paint and apparent glistening varnish on the surface," the report said.
But the tail end of another word on the stick was not readable, it said.
Her long blonde hair was entwined in the cord that was wrapped around her neck as well as in the cord wrapped around the stick.
The child's body was found by her father, John Ramsey, in the basement of the family's Boulder home on Dec. 26 in the afternoon and was then carried up to the living room.
The coroner arrived at 8 p.m. MST (10 p.m. EST).
The coroner said the child's body was "lying on her back with her arms extended up over her head." She was covered by a blanket and a sweatshirt when the coroner arrived.
A ransom note demanding $118,000 was found before dawn that day on the back staircase by the child's mother, Patsy, when she was on her way to the kitchen to make coffee.
The child was wearing long white underwear. The white panties she was wearing were decorated with printed rosebuds and the word "Wednesday" was on the waistband.
The report said the child's bladder was empty.
The autopsy report listed the cause of death as strangulation. The girl's skull was also fractured in the brutal attack.
No arrests have been made and no suspects named in the nearly 8-month-long investigation.
The Ramseys have criticized the police for focusing on them and have hired their own investigators. The parents have even taken out advertisements in Boulder newspapers asking the public for help.

Officials in Boulder had wanted to keep the autopsy under seal because they said it contained information only the killer would know. But media organizations challenged the coroner's office in court and the state Supreme Court ordered the report to be released.
